name: htan-the-cellular-geography-of-therapeutic-resistance-in-cancer
alternateName: The Cellular Geography of Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer
description:
Of the fourteen HTAN atlases, this is the one whose stated purpose is resistance: mapping where in a tumor resistant cells survive treatment. It carries 20,350 files across multiplexed tissue imaging, single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk DNA, and it is the only atlas in the network carrying the extended clinical data tier alongside therapy, follow-up, exposure, family history and molecular test components.
It is also the clearest case in this corpus of a resource that is well built and apparently unused. HTAN maintains its own publication manifest, and this atlas has no entry in it - unlike most atlases, which record three to five publications. The combination of a resistance-focused design, unusually complete clinical annotation and no recorded downstream use makes it the strongest reuse opportunity we identified.

supportedQuestions: Where within a tumor do cells that survive therapy actually reside?
Do spatial niches associated with resistance recur across cancer types, or are they tissue-specific?
Can the extended clinical tier be used to relate spatial organization to real treatment sequences rather than to treatment as a single binary?

blockingLimitations.statement: HTAN atlases profile few patients deeply. 20,350 files does not mean many participants, and participant counts are not exposed in the portal metadata.

inappropriateUses: Assuming clinical field completeness from their presence in the metadata.
